plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks negative profit while underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $4, which is quite low, I should bid exactly $4 to maximize expected profit and avoid overpaying if I win, or missing out on marginal profitable wins.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of beliefs about others' bids. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $23, bidding exactly $23 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid, which is optimal regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategy-proof. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - I cannot benefit from bidding higher or lower than my actual value of $32. If I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying relative to my value. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
